title: Brokoli worker capabilities v1 (ADR-033 section 5)
description: Canonical machine-readable contract for a worker's structured capability advertisement on registration and heartbeat -- authenticated observations, never author assertions. This is a rollout-phase-1 artifact (ADR-032/033 rollout, issue #439 step 5): it defines the advertisement shape only. No Go code reads, writes, persists, or matches against this shape yet -- there is no worker registration endpoint, no placement predicate, and this does not extend extensions.InstanceWorkOrder (ADR-017) in this phase. A change here is a change to every worker implementation and the control plane at once: version it accordingly, per the same discipline as task-interface-v1.json.

protocols.description: Every protocol this worker speaks, e.g. 'brokoli.instance/v2' (ADR-017) and 'brokoli.task-runtime/v1' (ADR-033 section 7). A worker missing a required protocol never receives work needing it -- absence fails closed.

runtimes.description: May be empty for a worker that speaks no task-runtime adapter at all (e.g. an ADR-029 code-node-only worker).

io.description: ADR-033 section 9's physical I/O modes this worker supports.

isolation.description: Isolation mechanisms this worker can enforce, e.g. 'process', 'container'. Deliberately not a closed enum -- ADR-033 section 12 names profiles (trusted/tenant/untrusted), not a fixed mechanism vocabulary; new mechanisms (namespaces, gVisor, ...) are expected to be added without a schema version bump to this array's contents.

labels.description: Free-form scheduling hints (e.g. {"accelerator": "none"}). Per ADR-033 section 5: labels may refine placement after compatibility is already proven, but can never substitute for runtime/protocol matching.

class.description: ADR-033 section 3's closed runtime-class vocabulary -- the same enum task-bundle-v2.json's payload.runtime uses.

versions.description: Concrete runtime versions installed on this worker, e.g. ['3.11.9', '3.12.4'] -- not a range. Range matching against a bundle payload's 'requires' happens at placement time, not here.

adapter.description: The runtime adapter's own version (ADR-033 section 15). Optional: a 'native' or 'container' runtime class may have no separate adapter version to report.
